ApiVersion.description: The major.minor version of the subordinate:plugin interface the plugin was built against, e.g. "0.1".

Capabilities.description:
`[capabilities]`: everything the sandbox opens only on request.

The manifest only *declares* these. Granting them is the install-time
approval step and enforcement is the host's, both in the crate's
`capability` module: an approval store records what the user approved, and
resolving it expands the roots into the sandbox's WASI preopens. Absent
keys mean "not requested", which is why parsing rejects unknown ones.

fs_read.description:
Roots the plugin may read, as `$PROJECT`-style roots or paths under
them.

network.description: Whether the plugin may open network connections.

shaders.description: Whether the plugin may have its WGSL shaders compiled and run.

changed.description:
False when it was already in that state, so a caller can tell a change
from a no-op.

enabled.description: Whether it is switched on now.

InstallLocation.description:
Where a plugin is installed.

The order is the precedence order: [`InstallLocation::Project`] is greater
than [`InstallLocation::User`] and wins an id conflict.

oneOf.description: The per-user plugin directory, shared by every project.

enabled.description: Whether it is switched on. Everything is on until switched off.

id.description: The identity from the manifest, which is the key everything uses.

location.description: Which of the two directories it was found in.

manifest.description:
Its whole parsed manifest, so a listing can show what it asks for
without reading the file again.

LoadFailure.description:
A plugin directory that could not be loaded.

Reported per plugin: the scan that produced it loaded every other plugin.
The three error fields are a [`SubError`] flattened, so the row carries a
stable code into JSON without the schema depending on the error type.

details.description: The error's details, e.g. the offending manifest field.

location.description: Which of the two directories it was found in.

capabilities.description: What the plugin asks to be allowed to do. Empty when absent.

mcp.description: The MCP tools the plugin contributes. Empty when absent.

plugin.description: Identity, interface version and the worlds implemented.

McpSection.description: `[mcp]`: the MCP tools the plugin contributes.

tools.description: Tools by name, as they appear to an agent.

description.description: What the tool does, used verbatim as the MCP tool description.

schema.description: The tool's input JSON Schema, relative to the plugin directory.

PluginSection.description: `[plugin]`: who the plugin is and what it implements.

api.description: The `subordinate:plugin` interface version it was built against.

description.description: One-sentence description, shown in the plugins panel.

Scan.description: Everything one walk of the plugin directories found.

failures.description: The directories that did not, sorted by path.

plugins.description: The plugins that loaded, sorted by id.

shadowed.description: The copies that lost an id conflict, sorted by path.

Shadowed.description:
A plugin that is installed but not loaded, because another copy of the same
id won.

directory.description: The directory of the copy that is *not* used.

shadowed_by.description: The directory of the copy that won.

World.description: A WIT world a plugin can implement (docs/PLAN.md §6.2).

oneOf.description: Parameters plus WGSL shaders, with an optional CPU fallback.
Block-based f32 audio processing under a real-time budget.
Turns a file or URL into media items or a sequence.
Encoder presets or a whole custom export target.
New editing commands built from Command API primitives.
Extra MCP tools the core forwards calls to.

methods.description: List every installed plugin, with the ones that failed to load and the ones hidden by an id conflict.
